paper_title: Can Language Models Follow Multiple Turns of Entangled Instructions

model_annotation: This nested donut chart represents the distribution of samples across three primary categories and nine specific capabilities. The chart consists of two concentric rings separated by thick white borders, totaling twelve distinct slices arranged around a hollow center. The inner ring contains three overarching categories labeled with bold white text directly inside the segments: "Contradiction Resolution" in brown, "Context Tracking" in dark blue, and "Context Retrieving" in dark teal. The outer ring is divided into nine sub-capability slices that visually correspond to the inner categories. These outer slices do not have percentage labels; instead, they are labeled outside the chart with black text and numerical sample counts connected by thin blue lines. Adjacent to "Contradiction Resolution" are "Prioritization" (light salmon, 100), "Personalization" (orange-red, 100), and "Privacy Protection" (bright red, 111). Aligned with "Context Tracking" are "Triggering" (light blue, 100), "Recursive Reasoning" (bright blue, 110), and "Dynamic Environment" (medium blue, 100). Finally, mapped to "Context Retrieving" are "Memorization" (light aquamarine, 100), "Dynamic Instruction" (turquoise, 100), and "Multitasking" (teal, 160). The chart lacks a separate legend, and while the segments are not ordered in a strict ascending or descending sequence, the widths of the outer slices visually correspond to their numerical values, notably with the "Multitasking" slice (160) appearing wider than the others.
